# Copy button: `jl-copy-button`

Copies a text to the clipboard, and says so.

- Class `JlCopyButton`, a molecule: `import { JlCopyButton } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/copy-button

Puts a text on the clipboard and turns into a check for a moment, so people know it worked. Code blocks
use it; use it beside any value people copy: a token, a link, a command.

## Use

```ts
import { JlCopyButton } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlCopyButton label="Copy" value="Hello from jlib" />
```

```html
<jl-copy-button label="Copy" value="Hello from jlib"></jl-copy-button>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `value` (attribute `value`): `string`, default `''`. The text to copy.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. Shown beside the icon; without it the button is an icon with a tooltip.
- `size` (attribute `size`): `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`, default `'sm'`. The height.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `copy` (`onCopy` in JSX), detail `string`: The text is on the clipboard.

## Methods

- `copy(): Promise<void>`: Copies the value now.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### Beside a value

```html
<div class="row">
  <code>npm install @syware/jlib</code>
  <jl-copy-button value="npm install @syware/jlib"></jl-copy-button>
</div>
```

### With a label

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-copy-button value="https://example.com/invite/7f3a" label="Copy link"></jl-copy-button>
  <jl-copy-button value="sk_live_51H" size="md" label="Copy key"></jl-copy-button>
</div>
```
